excerpt: Compare the cash required, net rental income, tenant fit and resale risks of a studio and a one-bedroom apartment in Ajman.
introduction:
A studio and a one-bedroom apartment can serve different tenants and require different amounts of capital. The better Ajman investment is not automatically the cheaper unit or the one with the highest advertised percentage. Compare two actual apartments with the same assumptions for rent, vacancy, operating costs and exit.

A studio may reduce the cash committed, while a one-bedroom can offer a separate living space and a different income profile. Those are possible trade-offs, not universal claims about demand or returns. Building quality, layout, ownership rights and the price you pay can change the result.
takeaways: Compare total acquisition cost, not just price per apartment or a developer's monthly payment headline.
Use comparable signed leases, vacancy and building-specific expenses to calculate net income.
Test the additional capital needed for a one-bedroom against the extra expected income and your exit plans.

sections.heading: What tenant need does each layout serve?
sections.body:
A studio combines principal living and sleeping functions in one space. Its usefulness depends on the actual floor plan: storage, natural light, ventilation, kitchen arrangement and privacy can matter as much as the advertised area. A one-bedroom separates sleeping from the main living space, but its corridor, kitchen or room proportions may still limit usable space. Inspect the unit or study the dimensioned plan rather than assuming a bedroom label guarantees a better layout.

Decide who the apartment is intended to serve and whether parking, work access, furnishings or building facilities matter to that tenant. The [Al Nuaimiya area guide](https://www.bayut.com/area-guides/al-nuaimiya/) and [Ajman Corniche guide](https://www.bayut.com/area-guides/ajman-corniche/) describe different urban and waterfront settings, but the tenant fit and competing supply must be assessed building by building.

Ask for comparable signed leases for the same type, condition, furnishing and payment terms. A listed asking rent does not prove the final rent or how quickly the apartment will be let.

table.caption: Questions to ask for each unit type
rows: Is there useful storage and a workable sleeping area?
Are the bedroom and living room usable as furnished?
What is the full price including acquisition and setup?
How much additional cash is required?
What have comparable studios actually rented for?
Does the additional rent justify the extra investment?
How many comparable studios compete in the building?
Can the owner cover costs during vacancy or repairs?
table.note: Neither column guarantees a particular tenant, occupancy or sale price.

sections.heading: A net-income comparison with sample numbers
sections.body:
Assume a studio costs AED 350,000 including acquisition charges, has headline annual rent of AED 30,000, a vacancy allowance of AED 2,500 and owner expenses of AED 6,500. Its sample annual net income is AED 21,000, equal to 6% of the total cost.

Assume a one-bedroom costs AED 550,000 in total, has headline annual rent of AED 42,000, a vacancy allowance of AED 3,500 and owner expenses of AED 8,500. Its sample net income is AED 30,000, or approximately 5.45% of cost. It produces AED 9,000 more income in the example but requires AED 200,000 more capital.

The additional AED 9,000 divided by the additional AED 200,000 is 4.5% before borrowing costs and tax. That comparison helps evaluate the extra capital, but it is not a forecast. Both examples use sample inputs, assume all remaining rent is collected and exclude finance, tax, major capital works and selling costs.

chart.note: Example inputs show how annual income and yield are calculated for each apartment. The one-bedroom also requires more capital in this example.

sections.heading: Which acquisition and operating costs matter?
sections.body:
Ask for the agreed unit price plus the buyer's registration, brokerage and other transaction charges. Include initial furnishing or repairs if the apartment needs them before it can be rented. The [Ajman sale-registration service](https://www.ajman.ae/en/servicecatalog/services/3162) sets out document and fee categories; request a current quote for the exact unit and parties because some displayed fee fields need clarification.

For annual costs, request service-charge statements and a management fee schedule. Add insurance, maintenance and any owner-paid utilities. Check whether cooling is billed separately and whether parking and furniture are included in the lease. A small unit does not necessarily carry lower charges per square foot, and a newer building does not eliminate maintenance.

Compare expenses on an annual basis and avoid double counting a vacancy allowance. A higher nominal rent is not enough if it comes with higher charges, more initial work or an excessive purchase premium.

sections.heading: How should financing affect the choice?
sections.body:
Calculate unleveraged net yield first: collected rent less owner operating expenses, divided by total acquisition cost. Then prepare a separate monthly cash-flow schedule with the actual mortgage repayment, bank fees and insurance. This keeps the underlying property's performance distinct from the effect of borrowing.

The larger apartment may require more cash at completion even if the lender finances part of the price. Check whether the bank's valuation supports the agreed purchase price, the rate after any fixed period and the terms for early settlement. If the valuation is lower than expected, the buyer may need to contribute more.

Test whether you can cover payments during vacancy and a repair. A projected positive annual yield can coexist with a month in which a mortgage payment and maintenance invoice exceed the rent received.

sections.heading: Compare resale and management risk
sections.body:
Look at actual completed sales of comparable units and the number of competing homes currently marketed in the same building. Asking prices are not completed transactions. Check whether any existing tenancy, outstanding service charges or financing could affect the timing of a future transfer.

The studio may require less capital in the example, but it is still one property exposed to a vacancy or repair. The one-bedroom may offer more annual income under the example assumptions, but the larger initial commitment leaves less capital available elsewhere. Neither format has a guaranteed resale market.

For an off-plan choice, ask for the registered project, the unit plan, payment and handover terms and any charges payable after completion. For a ready apartment, inspect the physical unit and shared areas and request the title and clearance details.

sections.heading: Choose using current evidence
sections.body:
Start with the [Ajman area guide](/journal/ajman-property-2026), then explore the [Aliyas Ajman project collection](/projects?emirate=Ajman) for projects matching your budget and preferred setting. Confirm the actual unit's availability, ownership right, price and payment schedule before calculating a return.

[Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget, intended holding period and preferred location. Ask for a studio and a one-bedroom comparison using the same assumptions, then verify the authority fee, service charges and comparable leases before making a decision.
